title: NIKATRU app declaration
description: apps/<id>/app.yaml — the ONE place an app's identity, hosts, platforms, storefront listings and legal URLs are written. catalog/apps.json, every apps/<id>/store/<channel>/{title,short-description,category,privacy-policy-url,support-url}.txt and the Apple channels' terms-of-use-url.txt are RENDERED from it by tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs; none of them is authored. [ADR 067] decision 2.

id.description: The app id, and the catalogue `slug`. The rule is contracts/app-id (lowercase letters and digits, a letter first, 2-32 characters); tooling/ci/assert-app-id-contract.mjs fails if this property accepts an id that contract refuses. Same shape assert-catalog-contract.mjs grades and the same string the directory is named.

name.description: The listing title. Rendered verbatim into every store/<channel>/title.txt and into the catalogue `name`, which is what makes them the same string by construction rather than by two spellings agreeing today. Play caps a title at 30 characters and it is the tightest of the five channels.

shortName.description: The ICON LABEL — what a home screen, a task switcher and a launcher show under the app's mark. It is NOT the store title: `name` is rendered into every store/<channel>/title.txt and into the catalogue, while this string is rendered into CFBundleDisplayName (iOS + macOS), android:label, the .desktop `Name=`, msix_config.display_name (which becomes uap:VisualElements/@DisplayName) and the PWA manifest `short_name` — the six places an operating system, rather than a store, has room for. OPTIONAL in this schema so an existing declaration still parses; tooling/ci/assert-app-naming.mjs is what REQUIRES it, caps it at 15 characters, requires it to share a whole token with `name`, and requires it to be unique across apps/*. Apple QA1892 asks that the device name and the store name be similar, which is why the shared token is a rule and not a preference. 15 rather than 30: iOS truncates a home-screen label around 12-13 glyphs and Android around 11-14, so anything longer is a label no user ever reads in full.

tagline.description: The one-line description. Rendered into every store/<channel>/short-description.txt and into the catalogue `tagline`. Play caps a short description at 80 characters.

category.description: The store category, rendered into every store/<channel>/category.txt. One word per the vocabulary the five consoles share.

status.description: The catalogue status. `preview` is what a stamp writes; `live` is a deliberate promotion. assert-catalog-contract.mjs admits exactly these two.

hosts.description: The app's own hosts, WITHOUT a scheme — the scheme is added by the renderer so that a catalogue row cannot carry http:// by a typo. A host here needs no HAND-MADE DNS record: a Worker route with custom_domain, or the web deployment, writes it. [ADR 006]'s proxied wildcard *.nikatru.com was the old reason and [ADR 080] section 4 deleted it on 2026-09-12.

web.description: The app's OWN ORIGIN host, e.g. subscriptiontracker-7qg.pages.dev. This is NOT the address the app is published at. Since [ADR 075] the published address is a PATH on the apex (https://nikatru.com/<id>), because a subdomain costs a payment-provider submission per app and a path costs nothing on either provider; this host survives as the origin the apex router proxies to, and as the source of the permanent 301. It needs no hand-made DNS record — the deployment binds it. ([ADR 006]'s proxied wildcard, which used to cover it, was deleted by [ADR 080] section 4 on 2026-09-12.)

pagesOrigin.description: The Cloudflare Pages PRODUCTION ALIAS of the app's own Direct Upload project, e.g. subscriptiontracker-7qg.pages.dev -- the host the apex router actually fetches. REQUIRED since 2026-09-27 (O-PRODUCT-RECORD-UNBUILT): tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs no longer falls back to `web`. It is declared rather than derived because it is NOT DERIVABLE: Cloudflare issues it when the project is created and appends a suffix when the name is taken, so guessing <id>.pages.dev is wrong for exactly the app this repository has. `node tooling/web/pages-origin.mjs --apply <id>` creates the project and prints it, the brick's `pages_origin` input writes it here, and `--check <id>` verifies it offline. deploy-web.yml's step "Prove app.yaml's pagesOrigin is the Pages project's own subdomain" runs `--verify <id>` before every deploy: it reads the subdomain back from Cloudflare and exits 1, publishing nothing, when this value differs. It is PREFERRED over `web` because *.pages.dev is OUTSIDE the nikatru.com zone, so the zone Redirect Rule that 301s the retired subdomain cannot match the router's own proxy subrequest -- a loop there takes the whole apex dark, marketing and the frozen legal archive with it.

api.description: The app's OWN API host, present only for an app with its own Worker. Absent or null means the app calls the shared platform Worker and the catalogue `api` is rendered as the empty string — which assert-catalog-contract.mjs requires to be PRESENT and permits to be EMPTY.

platforms.description: The platforms this app is actually built for. assert-catalog-contract.mjs cross-checks it against the channels a row claims a listing on, and assert-stamp-platforms.mjs against the build lanes.

listings.description: Storefront listing URLs, keyed by tooling/channel-register.json's `storefrontKey`. The KEY SET IS NOT DECLARED HERE: the renderer derives it from the register in register order, so adding a storefront is data rather than code ([ADR 055]). A key present here overrides; a key absent renders `null`, which is the honest answer until a store issues a real URL — inventing a plausible one publishes a link a stranger follows into a 404. `web` is derived from hosts.web and MUST NOT be written here. An empty block is written as `listings:` with nothing under it, which reads as null and means every store key renders null.

windows.description: OPTIONAL. What THIS app mints for itself on Windows — nothing a store console issues, which is why it is not in `stores.windows-store` (every key there but state/declaredOn is a console-issued id, tooling/store/store-record.mjs). ST-R4 (O-RENEWAL-REMINDERS-OFF-ON-DESKTOP): `toastActivatorClsid` is the CLSID of the COM activator a tapped toast launches; tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs writes it into msix_config.toast_activator.clsid AND into lib/core/windows_notification_identity.g.dart, so the packaged manifest and the running app name one activator. It is never reissued (a changed CLSID orphans every toast on screen). The brick derives it from the app id.

stores.description: OPTIONAL. What each store CONSOLE issued to this app, one closed record per store channel, keyed by the tooling/channel-register.json channel id and read through tooling/store/store-record.mjs storeRecordOf (the one reader; it never returns a default). O-SECOND-APP-SIGNS-AS-THE-FIRST limb (1): the Windows identity was one value on the windows-store channel row, and tooling/bricks/app/hooks/post_gen.dart copied that row into every app it stamped, so a second app would package and submit as the first. It is a top-level key and not `listings.windows-store.identity` because `listings` types every value as an https URL. The account-wide facts (`publisher`, `publisherDisplayName`) stay on the channel row. ⏱ 2026-09-25 (B4a-2): the channel row's copy is gone and this record is the one declaration of the app's Windows identity. tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs renders msix_config.identity_name from it, every Windows identity reader reads it through tooling/ci/read-identity.mjs windowsIdentityOf, and tooling/ci/assert-channel-register.mjs §6e recomputes its packageFamilyName from the row's publisher. ⏱ 2026-09-26 (O-STORE-RECORDS-ARE-ONE-PER-CHANNEL, 9a): every store channel has its record. Each carries `state` (pending: the console has not been read for every id; issued: it has) and `declaredOn` (null, or the date the owner swore THIS app's declarations in that console). TWO FACTS, NEVER MERGED (O-APP1-CONSOLE-DECLARATIONS-UNSUBMITTED): whether the store FILES are final or the brick's preview is each sworn file's own `sworn` key, graded by tooling/ci/assert-sworn-store-files.mjs; `declaredOn` gates a REAL submission only (that guard's --for-submission --real-submission). The bundle id and the Android package name are derived (tooling/apple-provisioning.json bundleIdOf; com.nikatru.<id>) and never stored. tooling/ci/assert-store-identity.mjs fails two apps sharing a record id, an iOS record id that is not the macOS one, and an issued record with a missing id.

windows-store.description: The MSIX Package/Identity/Name and the Package Family Name Partner Center issued to THIS app (Product → Product identity), and its Store ID. None can be derived from the app id. An app with no Partner Center product yet writes the channel row's `packageIdentity.notYetConfiguredSentinel`, PARTNER-CENTER-PENDING, in both identity fields: an invented value would package and submit under an identity nobody owns. `issued` needs all three, real.

declaredOn.description: null, or the date the owner swore this app's Partner Center declarations. Written only from the owner's word.

identityName.description: Letters, digits, `.` and `-`: the characters the one issued identity and the sentinel both use. The pattern refuses a space or an underscore typed into the field; it cannot tell a wrong name from a right one, which is what the equality checks are for.

packageFamilyName.description: `<identityName>_<publisher id>`, where the publisher id is 13 lower-case Crockford base32 characters (tooling/ci/assert-channel-register.mjs §6e derives it from the publisher), or the sentinel.

productId.description: The Partner Center Store ID (Product → Product identity → Store ID), twelve upper-case letters and digits. It replaces the MS_STORE_PRODUCT_ID secret read (9b). Absent while `pending`.

ios-appstore.description: The App Store Connect record (its Apple ID, digits). ONE record covers iOS and macOS (the register's macos-appstore row), so tooling/ci/assert-store-identity.mjs requires this recordId to equal stores.macos-appstore.recordId. Absent while `pending`.

declaredOn.description: null, or the date the owner swore this app's App Store Connect App Privacy and age-rating answers.

recordId.description: The App Store Connect Apple ID, quoted so YAML reads it as text.

macos-appstore.description: The same App Store Connect record as ios-appstore, written twice so a per-channel reader needs no cross-channel rule; tooling/ci/assert-store-identity.mjs fails the two disagreeing.

android-play.description: The Play APP SIGNING certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint(s) (Play Console → Setup → App signing), not the upload key: the one an assetlinks.json must name. Play App Signing has no key before the first upload, so a new app is `pending` with none. The package name is com.nikatru.<id>, derived and never stored.

declaredOn.description: null, or the date the owner swore this app's Play Data safety, content-rating and ads declarations.

linux-snap.description: The Snap Store record. The snap name is derived (apps/<id>/store/linux-snap/snap-name.txt, graded by assert-store-identity), so the record is its state alone: issued once `snapcraft register` has reserved the name for this app.

apps-gov-in.description: The apps.gov.in (Mobile Seva AppStore, Government of India) record. The portal publishes no submission API and each app is its own listing, created by hand in the authenticated portal (tooling/channel-register.json `apps-gov-in` noSubmissionApi), so the record is its state alone: issued once the owner's upload has created THIS app's listing. ⏱ 2026-10-01 (rv2-newproduct-012, AA-16, O-STORE-RECORDS-ARE-ONE-PER-CHANNEL): it was the one store channel with no per-app record, so app #2 had nowhere to say whether its listing exists and tooling/ci/assert-store-identity.mjs counted none. The signing pin is NOT here: one key (alias nikatru-appsgovin) is decided for the channel (the row's `signing`), and whether a second app signs with it or with a key of its own is the owner's custody decision.

legal.description: The listing URLs. privacyPolicyUrl and supportUrl go into every channel's tree; termsUrl (added 2026-09-24, O-APPLE-LISTING-HAS-NO-EULA) goes only into the channels whose register row names terms-of-use-url.txt in its additionalFiles, today the two Apple rows. All three are compared to tooling/channel-register.json's storeMetadataContract.portfolioUrls by assert-store-metadata.mjs, so a fork here fails the build rather than pointing a store reviewer at somebody else's policy.

markets.description: The markets this app is offered in. Optional, and rendered into the catalogue row only when declared — the shipped row for the one live app carries none, and adding an empty field would change bytes the live site serves for no reason. [pipeline K-1/K-16].

billing.description: OPTIONAL. Present only for an app that sells through a STORE billing rail on mobile — [ADR 067] decision 7, [ADR 039] D2/D3/D5. Absent means the app sells through the merchant-of-record hosted checkout on the channels that permit it and sells nothing on Play or the App Store, which is [ADR 059] shape A. ⏱ O-BRICK-SELLS-NOTHING-IN-A-STORE (12a): the declaration can be `state: pending` before the owner creates the app's RevenueCat apps, so an app can opt in before it can sell. Declaring it is an OPT-IN with consequences a guard holds: tooling/ci/assert-app-yaml.mjs limb 6 requires the app's pubspec to depend on nikatru_billing_revenuecat, its store/android-play/data-safety.json to swear Purchase history, and its store/ios-appstore/privacy-manifest.json to carry the SDK's rows — and requires the reverse, so the dependency cannot arrive without the declaration either.

mobileIap.description: The store IAP configuration. Holds NO SECRET: the RevenueCat app ids below are public identifiers, and the SDK's public key is supplied at runtime by the app rather than written here — a key in a declaration is a key in git.

provider.description: The IAP provider. One value today, and an enum rather than a free string so a second provider is a schema change somebody reviews rather than a typo that reads as adoption.

entitlementId.description: The entitlement identifier configured in the provider's dashboard, e.g. 'pro'. The SAME name our own entitlement record uses, because the client only reports what the store says and the server is what grants.

revenuecatAppIds.description: The provider's own app id per platform. Both are required: an app that declares mobile IAP with only one is an app whose other store build would configure the SDK against nothing and refuse every purchase with no reason a user could act on.

state.description: O-BRICK-SELLS-NOTHING-IN-A-STORE (12a). `live`: the owner created the app's two RevenueCat apps, so `revenuecatAppIds` is REQUIRED and routes its events (render.mjs renders them into revenuecat-app-ids.ts). `pending`: nothing is created yet, so `revenuecatAppIds` must be ABSENT — never a placeholder, because a fake id would render into that routing map. A pending app builds keyless and fail-closed, and is never submitted to a store (assert-app-yaml --for-submission).

publicKeySecrets.description: The NAMES of the two repository secrets that hold this app's RevenueCat PUBLIC SDK keys, one per store. A name, never a value (this block holds no secret). Store builds resolve the name for the job's app through tooling/ci/store-key-secret.mjs, and channel-register `purchaseRails.storeKeyDefine.secretFieldByRail` says which field a rail reads. A name is one app's: render.mjs refuses one name in two apps, because a RevenueCat key belongs to ONE RevenueCat app.

storeProducts.description: The store subscription products this app sells in-app: one per plan, and the SAME developer-chosen product id on Play and the App Store ([ADR 093] §2). `plan` has no lifetime: [ADR 093] §2 never sells it in-app. render.mjs refuses a plan listed twice and, at `live`, a plan missing.

anyOf.description: live: the RevenueCat apps exist, so their ids are declared.
pending: nothing is issued yet, so no RevenueCat app id is declared.

audience.description: The declared audience. Optional in the same way as `markets`. ADR 068 sets the floor at 18 for every NIKATRU product, so nothing here may describe a child audience.

ai.description: REQUIRED of every app, `false` included: a claim with neither a derivation nor an owner fails, and an absent key would read as 'no' while nobody said so. O-PLAY-AI-CONTENT-REPORTING. Google Play's AI-Generated Content policy (answer/13985936, read 2026-09-18) requires an in-app report control in any app that generates content with AI. tooling/ci/assert-app-yaml.mjs limb 7 holds the consequences both ways: true requires AppConfig.generatesAiContent, the wired ReportContentDialog, and a Data safety answer for table:platform_db.content_reports; false requires the content-rating `generates-ai-content` dependency-tells claim, which fails the day a direct AI package arrives.

generatesContent.description: Whether the app generates content with AI at runtime — text, images, voice or video a model produces for the user. Out of Play's scope: an app that only hosts AI content, summarises non-AI content, or uses AI to improve an existing productivity feature (answer/14094294).

exportCompliance.description: REQUIRED of every app, `false` included, for the reason `ai` is: an optional field the renderer defaulted to false would be a legal declaration nobody made. O-APPLE-PLIST-KEYS-UNRENDERED. tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs renders `usesNonExemptEncryption` into ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption in both Apple Info.plists, and tooling/ci/assert-app-yaml.mjs limb 8 (export-compliance consistency) holds a `false` to the code: no shipped first-party Dart may import a cipher package or name a cipher class, and the app's pubspec may carry no direct dependency on one.

usesNonExemptEncryption.description: Apple's export-compliance answer, as the build ships it. `false` means every use of cryptography in the app falls inside Apple's exemption (OS-provided HTTPS, authentication, digital signatures, hashing). The owner answers App Store Connect's export questions consistently with it.

basis.description: The sentence a reviewer reads: what was measured and why the answer holds. A stamped app carries the brick's placeholder, marked to be re-measured before its first Apple upload.
